note: Original starter recipes shipped with the app, written for Mise and not copied from anywhere. Section 5.1 asks for 40 to 60; this batch brings it to 45. Every ingredient links to a canonical item so the grocery list works on first launch, and every step lists its own ingredients for cook mode.

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Salmon and Green Beans
recipes.summary: Salmon and green beans roast together on one pan while the oven does the work.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F and put a sheet pan inside while it heats.
Toss the green beans with half the oil, the garlic, and a big pinch of salt.
Pat the salmon dry, rub it with the rest of the oil, and season it well.
Spread the beans on the hot pan, set the salmon on top, and roast until the fish flakes, about 12 to 14 minutes.
Squeeze the lemon over everything before serving.

recipes.title: Fast Shrimp Tacos
recipes.summary: Shrimp cook in four minutes, so dinner lands about as fast as the tortillas warm.

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, sriracha, and the juice of one lime together. Thin it with a little water if it is stiff.
Toss the cabbage with the juice of the other lime and a pinch of salt. Let it sit while you cook.
Toss the shrimp with the oil and chili powder, then cook in a hot skillet until pink, about 2 minutes a side.
Warm the tortillas, then build with shrimp, slaw, sauce, and plenty of cilantro.

recipes.title: Lemon Garlic Butter Pasta
recipes.summary: Five pantry things and one pot. The pasta water does the saucing.

steps.text: Boil the pasta in well salted water. Save a mug of the water before you drain it.
Melt the butter with the garlic and pepper flakes over low heat until the garlic smells sweet, about 2 minutes. Do not let it brown.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of the saved water, then toss hard until it turns glossy.
Off the heat, add the parmesan, the zest and juice of the lemon, and the parsley.

recipes.title: Crispy Chickpea Bowls
recipes.summary: Chickpeas crisp in a skillet, then land on rice with a lemon yogurt sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice.
Dry the chickpeas well, then fry them in the oil over medium high heat until they crackle and brown, about 10 minutes.
Add the cumin and paprika to the pan and toss for 30 seconds.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Build bowls with rice, chickpeas, cucumber, and the sauce spooned over.

recipes.title: Miso Butter Cod
recipes.summary: A miso butter melts over cod under the broiler. Four ingredients, eight minutes.

steps.text: Start the rice and heat the broiler.
Mash the miso into the butter until smooth.
Set the cod on a lined pan, spread the miso butter over the top, and broil until it browns and flakes, 7 to 9 minutes.
Scatter the scallions over and serve on the rice.

recipes.title: Black Bean Quesadillas
recipes.summary: The one everyone eats. Crisp outside, molten inside, ready in fifteen.

steps.text: Mash half the beans with the cumin and a splash of water so they hold together.
Spread the mash on four tortillas, add the whole beans and the cheese, and top with the rest.
Cook in a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat until golden and melted, about 3 minutes a side.
Cut into wedges and serve with the salsa.

recipes.title: Coconut Curry Lentils
recipes.summary: Red lentils collapse into a curry in twenty minutes with no soaking.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil over medium heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder and stir for a minute until fragrant.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk, and broth. Simmer until the lentils fall apart, about 18 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then season to taste.

recipes.title: Sesame Soba Noodles
recipes.summary: Cold noodles in a sesame dressing. Good hot, better the next day from the fridge.

steps.text: Boil the soba, then rinse under cold water so it stops sticking.
Whisk the sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, and honey together.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, cucumber, and most of the scallions.
Finish with the sesame seeds and the rest of the scallions.

recipes.title: Tomato and White Bean Soup
recipes.summary: A pantry soup that tastes slow cooked after twenty five minutes.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil until soft and sweet, about 8 minutes.
Add the oregano, tomatoes, beans, and broth. Simmer 15 minutes.
Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken it.
Serve with parmesan on top and toasted bread alongside.

recipes.title: Greek Salad Pita Plates
recipes.summary: No cooking at all. Chop, stir, warm the pita, done.

steps.text: Soak the red onion in cold water for 5 minutes so it loses its bite, then drain.
Toss the cucumber, tomato, and onion with the oil, vinegar, and oregano.
Crumble the feta over the top and let it sit while you warm the pita.
Serve with the yogurt for dipping and the warm pita for scooping.

recipes.title: Charred Broccoli Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Broccoli roasted hard until the edges go dark, on rice with a soy honey glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 450F and start the rice.
Toss the broccoli with the vegetable oil and roast until the edges char, about 20 minutes.
Warm the soy sauce, honey, garlic, and sesame oil in a small pan until it thickens slightly.
Toss the hot broccoli in the glaze, pile it on the rice, and finish with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Weeknight Chicken Stir Fry
recipes.summary: Everything chopped before the pan gets hot, then five minutes of cooking.

steps.text: Start the rice. Chop everything before you turn on the skillet, because there is no time once it is hot.
Stir the soy sauce, cornstarch, and a splash of water together and set it by the stove.
Sear the chicken in the oil over high heat until browned, about 5 minutes, then move it to a plate.
Cook the pepper and snap peas for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce, and toss until it coats everything. Finish with scallions over the rice.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Rice
recipes.summary: Cold rice, eggs, and peas come together in one hot pan in ten minutes.

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Add the carrot and garlic and cook until they soften, about 2 minutes.
Push everything to one side, crack in the eggs, and scramble them.
Add the rice and peas and press them flat so they crisp, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, and scallions and serve.

recipes.title: Skillet Caprese Pasta
recipes.summary: Fresh mozzarella and basil melt into hot pasta and burst tomatoes.

steps.text: Boil the spaghetti in salted water until just tender, then save a cup of the water.
Warm the olive oil and garlic in a skillet until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they burst, about 6 minutes.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of its water, the salt, and pepper.
Off the heat, fold in the mozzarella and basil so it just melts.

recipes.title: Tuna and White Bean Salad
recipes.summary: A no-cook lunch or light dinner built from the pantry.

steps.text: Flake the tuna into a bowl with the beans, onion, and parsley.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, mustard, and salt into a dressing.
Pour it over the salad and toss gently so the beans stay whole.

recipes.title: Shrimp Scampi Linguine
recipes.summary: Garlicky butter and lemon coat shrimp and pasta in one quick pan.

steps.text: Boil the linguine in salted water until just tender.
Melt the butter with the olive oil, garlic, and pepper flakes in a skillet.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink, about 3 minutes a side.
Toss in the pasta, lemon juice, and parsley with a splash of pasta water.

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Peppers
recipes.summary: Sausage and sweet peppers roast on one pan for an easy dinner.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F.
Toss the peppers and onion with the olive oil, seasoning, and salt on a sheet pan.
Nestle the sausages among the vegetables.
Roast until the sausages are browned and the peppers are soft, about 22 minutes.

recipes.title: Chickpea Coconut Curry
recipes.summary: A cozy simmer of chickpeas and tomato in coconut milk over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by the package directions.
Soften the onion, garlic, and ginger in the oil in a pot.
Stir in the curry powder for a minute, then add the tomatoes and coconut milk.
Add the chickpeas and simmer until thickened, about 12 minutes.
Wilt in the spinach and serve over the rice.

recipes.title: Baked Feta Pasta
recipes.summary: Feta and tomatoes roast into a creamy sauce you stir through pasta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400F.
Put the feta in the middle of a dish, surround it with tomatoes and garlic, and coat with oil and pepper flakes.
Roast until the tomatoes burst and the feta is soft, about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile boil the penne until tender.
Mash everything into a sauce, then fold in the pasta and basil.

recipes.title: Ground Turkey Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: A savory sweet turkey skillet spooned over rice with quick cucumbers.

steps.text: Cook the jasmine rice by the package directions.
Brown the turkey in the oil, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the soy sauce, honey, and sriracha.
Simmer until glazed, about 4 minutes.
Serve over rice with the cucumber and scallions.

recipes.title: Honey Soy Salmon Bowls
recipes.summary: Salmon glazed in a three-ingredient sauce over rice and greens.

steps.text: Cook the white rice by the package directions.
Stir the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, and garlic into a glaze.
Sear the salmon in the oil, then brush on the glaze and let it bubble.
Steam or roast the broccoli until bright and just tender.
Serve the salmon and broccoli over rice with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Broccoli Cheddar Soup
recipes.summary: A smooth, cheesy soup that even broccoli skeptics finish.

steps.text: Melt the butter and soften the onion in a pot.
Stir in the flour for a minute, then whisk in the broth and milk.
Add the broccoli and carrot and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar and salt until smooth.

recipes.title: Pesto Shrimp Couscous
recipes.summary: Pantry pesto ties together shrimp, couscous, and tomatoes fast.

steps.text: Cook the couscous by the package directions and fluff it.
Sear the shrimp in the olive oil with the salt until pink.
Add the tomatoes and warm them through.
Fold the couscous and pesto into the pan and finish with lemon.

recipes.title: Black Bean and Egg Skillet
recipes.summary: Eggs baked into spiced black beans and tomatoes for any meal.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil, then stir in the cumin and paprika.
Add the beans and tomatoes and simmer until saucy, about 6 minutes.
Make wells and crack in the eggs, then cover and cook until set.
Scatter cilantro and feta over the top.

recipes.title: Sausage, Kale, and White Bean Soup
recipes.summary: A hearty one-pot soup that tastes like it took all day.

steps.text: Brown the sausage in the oil, breaking it up.
Add the onion, garlic, and carrot and cook until soft.
Pour in the broth and beans and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the kale and salt and cook until wilted.

recipes.title: Miso Edamame Soba
recipes.summary: A warm bowl of soba in gingery miso broth with edamame.

steps.text: Bring the broth and ginger to a simmer.
Cook the soba in the broth until tender, then add the edamame and carrot.
Take the pot off the heat and whisk in the miso so it does not boil.
Finish each bowl with scallions and sesame oil.

recipes.title: Lemon Chicken Orzo
recipes.summary: Chicken and orzo simmer together into a bright one-pot dinner.

steps.text: Season and sear the chicken in the oil, then set it aside.
Toast the orzo and garlic in the same pan for a minute.
Add the broth, return the chicken, and simmer until the orzo is tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the spinach, lemon, and parmesan.

recipes.title: Ground Beef Taco Skillet
recipes.summary: Everything in a taco, cooked in one pan and scooped with chips.

steps.text: Brown the beef, then drain off the extra fat.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin for a minute.
Add the beans, corn, and salsa and simmer for 5 minutes.
Melt the cheddar on top and finish with cilantro, with chips for scooping.

recipes.title: Coconut Shrimp Curry
recipes.summary: Shrimp poached in a fragrant coconut curry over rice.

steps.text: Cook the jasmine rice by the package directions.
Fry the curry paste and garlic in the oil until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the pepper, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Slip in the shrimp and cook until pink, about 4 minutes.
Finish with lime and cilantro and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Tomatoes
recipes.summary: Cod bakes over garlicky tomatoes and olives in one dish.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400F.
Scatter the tomatoes, olives, and garlic in a dish and coat with oil.
Nestle the cod on top and season it with salt.
Bake until the fish flakes, about 16 minutes.
Finish with lemon and parsley.

recipes.title: Spinach Ricotta Pasta
recipes.summary: Creamy ricotta and wilted spinach make a five-minute sauce.

steps.text: Boil the rigatoni until tender and save some pasta water.
Wilt the spinach with the garlic in the oil.
Stir in the ricotta and a splash of pasta water to loosen it.
Fold in the pasta, parmesan, lemon, and salt.

recipes.title: Chicken Fajita Bowls
recipes.summary: Seared chicken and peppers over rice with all the fixings.

steps.text: Cook the white rice by the package directions.
Toss the chicken with the chili powder and cumin, then sear it in the oil.
Add the peppers and onion and cook until charred at the edges.
Squeeze lime over the pan and serve over rice with sliced avocado.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos
recipes.summary: Roasted sweet potato and beans folded into warm tortillas.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F.
Toss the sweet potato with the oil, chili powder, and cumin and roast for 20 minutes.
Add the beans to the pan for the last 5 minutes to warm through.
Fill the tortillas and top with avocado, lime, and cilantro.

recipes.title: Egg Drop Ramen
recipes.summary: Silky egg ribbons in a quick gingery ramen broth.

steps.text: Simmer the broth with the ginger and soy sauce.
Cook the ramen in the broth until just tender.
Stir the broth into a swirl and pour in the beaten eggs so they ribbon.
Add the spinach, then finish with scallions and sesame oil.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.summary: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, scooped with bread.

steps.text: Soften the onion, pepper, and garlic in the oil.
Stir in the cumin and paprika, then add the tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes.
Make wells and crack in the eggs, then cover until the whites set.
Scatter feta over the top and serve with the baguette.

recipes.title: Salmon Cakes
recipes.summary: Crisp pan-fried cakes from canned salmon and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Flake the salmon into a bowl with the panko, egg, mayo, mustard, and scallions.
Form the mix into patties.
Fry them in the oil until golden, about 4 minutes a side.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Veggie Quinoa Stir Fry
recipes.summary: Cooked quinoa crisped in a hot pan with edamame and egg.

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil and cook the carrot, pepper, and garlic until crisp-tender.
Push them aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the quinoa and edamame and press them flat to crisp, about 4 minutes.
Finish with soy sauce and sesame oil.

recipes.title: Sesame Chicken and Broccoli
recipes.summary: A glossy takeout-style stir fry that beats delivery on time.

steps.text: Cook the white rice by the package directions.
Toss the chicken with the cornstarch, then sear it in the oil until golden.
Add the broccoli and garlic and stir fry until bright.
Pour in the soy sauce, honey, and vinegar and toss until glazed.
Scatter sesame seeds and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Creamy Tomato Penne
recipes.summary: A quick blush sauce of tomato and cream over penne.

steps.text: Boil the penne until tender.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes, then stir in the cream.
Toss the pasta through with the parmesan, salt, and basil.

recipes.title: Kimchi Fried Rice
recipes.summary: Tangy kimchi fries up with rice and a runny egg on top.

steps.text: Fry the kimchi in the vegetable oil until it caramelizes.
Stir in the gochujang, then add the rice and press it flat to crisp.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil and pile onto plates.
Fry the eggs and set one on each bowl with scallions.

recipes.title: Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Bowls
recipes.summary: Crispy roasted cauliflower and chickpeas over grains with tahini.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F and cook the farro by the package directions.
Toss the cauliflower and chickpeas with the oil, cumin, and paprika.
Roast until crisp and browned, about 25 minutes.
Whisk the tahini and lemon with a little water into a drizzle.
Build bowls of farro, vegetables, tahini, and parsley.

recipes.title: Crispy Cod Tacos
recipes.summary: Golden cod in warm tortillas with a quick cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Cut the cod into strips, dip them in egg, then coat in panko.
Fry them in the oil until golden and crisp, about 3 minutes a side.
Toss the cabbage with the mayo, lime, and cilantro for a slaw.
Fill the tortillas with cod and slaw.

recipes.title: Cheesy Black Bean Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
recipes.summary: Baked sweet potatoes loaded with spiced beans and cheddar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F, prick the sweet potatoes, and roast until soft, about 40 minutes.
Warm the beans with the oil, cumin, and chili powder.
Split the potatoes and fill them with beans and cheddar, then return them until it melts.
Top with yogurt and scallions.

recipes.title: Open Face Tuna Melts
recipes.summary: Bubbly cheddar over lemony tuna on toasted sourdough.

steps.text: Heat the broiler.
Mix the tuna with the mayo, mustard, celery, and lemon.
Pile it onto slices of sourdough and cover with cheddar.
Broil until the cheese bubbles, about 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Crispy Gnocchi Tomato Skillet
recipes.summary: Pantry gnocchi crisped and simmered with tomatoes and mozzarella.

steps.text: Grate and squeeze the potato dry, then crisp it in the oil as rough gnocchi.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes, then the tomatoes and salt.
Simmer until saucy, about 10 minutes.
Scatter mozzarella over the top and cover until it melts, then add basil.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Dal
recipes.summary: A pot of soft red lentils with warm spice that is better on day two and feeds a week of bowls.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils in a few changes of cold water until the water stops going cloudy, then drain them. This is the difference between dal that tastes clean and dal that tastes dusty.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until it is soft and starting to brown at the edges, about 8 minutes. Browning here is most of the flavor, so give it the time.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for a minute, until the raw edge is gone.

Add the turmeric, cumin, and pepper flakes and stir them in the hot oil for about 30 seconds, until they smell toasted. Keep them moving so they do not catch and turn bitter. The garam masala is held back until the end.
Add the tomatoes and cook them down for 4 or 5 minutes, until the mixture is thick and jammy and no longer smells like a tin.

Add the lentils, the broth, and the salt. Bring it to a boil, then turn it down to a low simmer and leave it partly covered for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks to the bottom. It is done when the lentils have given up their shape entirely, which can take 5 minutes longer if the lentils have been in the cupboard a while.

While it simmers, rinse the rice and cook it in a saucepan with one and a half times its volume of water, so about 2 and a quarter cups here. Twice the water, which is the habit most of us have from other rice, leaves basmati soggy. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes before you fluff it.

Stir the butter and the garam masala into the dal over low heat for a minute, then take the pot off the heat, squeeze in the juice of a whole lemon, and taste for salt. The garam masala goes in now rather than at the start because its aroma cooks off over a long simmer. Loosen the dal with a splash of water if it is thicker than you want, or simmer it uncovered a few minutes if it is thinner, aiming a little looser than you mean to serve it because it firms up as it stands. A spoonful of olive oil in place of the butter keeps it vegan, and low sodium broth will want another half teaspoon of salt.

Serve it as parts rather than as plates: rice and a ladle of dal in each bowl, and the yogurt, cilantro, scallions, the second lemon in wedges, and warm naan set out for people to add themselves. Plain dal over plain rice is a complete dinner for whoever wants it that way.

It keeps 5 days covered in the fridge and is better on the second day, once the spices have settled. It sets thick when cold, so reheat it in a pot over low heat with a splash of water, stirring until it is loose again, and wake it up with fresh lemon. It also freezes for 3 months in meal-sized containers; thaw overnight in the fridge, or reheat straight from frozen over low heat with a little extra water and a lid.

recipes.title: Frittata
recipes.summary: Eggs, whatever vegetable is going, and a cheese, set in a skillet and finished in the oven. As good cold as warm.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375F with a rack in the middle.

Beat the eggs with the milk, 1 teaspoon of the salt, and plenty of pepper until the yolks and whites are one color, then stir in two thirds of the cheese. Any firm cheese that melts works here, and a hard grating cheese works too.

Warm the oil in a ten inch oven safe skillet over medium high heat and cook the onion until it is limp and translucent, about 4 minutes. It will not be sweet and caramelized in that time and does not need to be.

Add the zucchini and the last quarter teaspoon of salt, spread it in one layer, and cook with little stirring until the water it throws off has boiled away and some slices have browned edges, 6 to 8 minutes. The pan should look dry before the eggs go anywhere near it. Whatever vegetable is in the drawer goes here instead: spinach wilted and squeezed hard, leftover roasted vegetables, cooked potato in cubes, halved cherry tomatoes. The only rule is that it goes in cooked and dry, because raw wet vegetables make a weepy frittata.
Spread the vegetables level, pour the eggs over, and leave the pan alone for two minutes, until the edge has begun to set.

Scatter the rest of the cheese over the top and slide the skillet into the oven. Bake until the middle is just set and barely trembles when you nudge the handle, 10 to 14 minutes. Pull it while the center still looks a shade underdone; it firms up as it rests.

Rest it 5 minutes, run a spatula around the edge, and slide it onto a board to cut into wedges. Scatter the parsley. Put the salami on its own plate so whoever wants it can lay it over their own slice.

Cooled and wrapped, it keeps four days in the fridge and is genuinely good cold, straight from it, which is the whole reason to make a big one. To warm a wedge, give it 10 minutes in a 300F oven or two minutes in a dry covered skillet over low heat. The microwave turns it rubbery.

recipes.title: Chana Masala
recipes.summary: Chickpeas simmered down in a deeply cooked onion and tomato masala, better on day two and built to be spooned over rice at the table.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion with a pinch of the salt, stirring now and then, until it is soft and the edges have gone properly brown, 12 to 15 minutes. This browning is where most of the flavor comes from, so give it the time rather than rushing to the spices.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for a minute, until the raw smell is gone.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and the cayenne if you want heat. Stir them into the oil for about 30 seconds so they toast rather than steam.

Stir in the tomato paste, then the tomatoes and the rest of the salt. Cook at a lively simmer until the mixture darkens and pulls together and you can see the oil coming back out at the edges, 8 to 10 minutes.

Add the chickpeas and a cup of water. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, then crush a ladleful of the chickpeas against the side of the pot and stir them back in, which thickens the whole thing without any cream.
Cook the rice by the package directions while the chickpeas simmer.
Off the heat, stir in the garam masala and a squeeze of lemon. Taste for salt, and add more lemon until it tastes bright rather than flat.
Put the pot, the rice, and the cilantro, yogurt, lemon wedges, and warmed naan out separately so everyone builds their own plate.

Cooled and covered, it keeps five days in the fridge and is better on day two. Reheat in a pot over low heat with a splash of water to loosen it, stirring until it is hot through, about 8 minutes, and finish with fresh lemon.

recipes.title: White Bean and Kale Soup
recipes.summary: A pot of beans and greens that is better on day two and asks nothing of you on the night you eat it.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot, and celery with a pinch of the salt until they are soft and sweet, about 10 minutes. This slow start is where the broth gets its body, so do not hurry it.
Add the garlic, thyme, and red pepper flakes and stir for a minute, until the garlic smells like something you want to eat but has taken no color.

Tip in the beans and the broth, drop in the bay leaves and the parmesan rind if you have one, and bring it to a gentle simmer. Cook 20 minutes, which is long enough for the rind to give up its salt and the beans to stop tasting of the tin.
Crush a ladleful of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them back in. That is the whole thickening trick, and it works better than flour or cream because it tastes of the soup.
Stir in the kale and simmer until it is tender but still dark green, about 5 minutes. Fish out the bay leaves and the rind, then taste and correct with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
If anyone wants the sausage, brown it in a skillet while the soup finishes, break it up, and keep it in its own bowl so it never touches the pot.

Put the pot on the table with the grated parmesan, the lemon wedges, bread, and the sausage all in separate bowls, and let everybody finish their own. A child who wants beans and broth and nothing green can have exactly that, and the lemon is what makes an adult bowl taste bright rather than worthy.

It keeps five days in the fridge and is better on the second, once the starch has thickened the broth. Reheat it gently on the stove with a splash of water or broth, since it sets up overnight. It freezes for three months: freeze it before the kale goes in if you are planning ahead, or accept softer kale later.

recipes.title: Baked Ziti
recipes.summary: Pasta, marinara, and three cheeses layered in a dish that can wait two days in the fridge before it ever sees the oven.

steps.text: Boil the pasta in well salted water, but pull it two minutes before it is tender. It finishes cooking in the sauce in the oven, and pasta boiled all the way goes soft there. Drain it and toss it with a spoonful of the oil so it does not set into a block.

Warm the rest of the oil in a skillet with the garlic and the red pepper flakes until the garlic smells sweet, about a minute, then pour in the marinara with the oregano and let it bubble gently for five minutes. This is what makes a jar of sauce taste like someone cooked it.
In a bowl, beat the ricotta with the egg, half the parmesan, the salt, the pepper, and half the basil. The egg is what keeps the ricotta in soft pockets instead of letting it run out into the sauce.
Stir most of the sauce through the drained pasta, keeping about a cup back.

Spread a thin layer of the reserved sauce in the baking dish. Add half the pasta, drop half the ricotta over it in spoonfuls, and scatter on a third of the mozzarella. Repeat with the rest of the pasta and ricotta, then spread the last of the sauce on top and finish with the remaining mozzarella and parmesan.
For the one who wants meat, brown the sausage in its own pan, break it up, and keep it in a bowl on the table to spoon over a plate. Leaving it out of the dish means everyone can eat the same pan.

Cover the dish with foil and bake at 375F for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake another 15 until the edges bubble and the top has brown spots. Let it sit for 10 minutes before cutting or the first serving slides apart. Scatter the rest of the basil over the top.

To make it ahead, stop after the layering: covered tightly, the unbaked dish keeps two days in the fridge, and goes into the oven straight from cold with 15 minutes added to the covered time. Baked, it keeps four days covered in the fridge and three months frozen. Reheat a portion covered at 350F for about 20 minutes, or in the microwave with a spoonful of water over it to bring the steam back.

recipes.title: Make-Ahead Shakshuka
recipes.summary: A pepper and tomato base that keeps a week in the fridge, so dinner is eight minutes of poaching eggs.

steps.text: Cook the onion and peppers in the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until they slump and pick up a little color, 12 to 15 minutes. The slow start is the whole difference between this and a jar of tomato sauce, so give it the time.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and pepper flakes and cook for a minute, until they smell toasted rather than dusty. Add the tomato paste and keep stirring until it darkens a shade.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the salt, and the pepper. Simmer until the sauce holds its shape on a spoon instead of running off it, 15 to 20 minutes, then taste it and salt it again if it needs it.

This is where the recipe is meant to stop. Cool the base and put it in a jar in the fridge, and a busy night later this week is eight minutes of work instead of forty. Doubling the base costs nothing but a bigger pan, so do that while the board is already dirty.
To eat: bring the base back to a lively simmer in a wide skillet, loosening it with a splash of water if the fridge has stiffened it. It should be bubbling before the eggs go anywhere near it.

Make eight shallow wells with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Salt the tops, cover the pan, and cook over low heat until the whites set and the yolks still wobble, about 8 minutes. Pull them a shade early, because the hot sauce keeps cooking them at the table.
Brown the chorizo in a small dry skillet and tip it into its own bowl, for whoever wants it on their plate.

Take the pan to the table with the feta, the parsley, and torn bread in separate bowls, so everyone lifts out their own egg and adds only what they want. The base keeps a week in the fridge and three months frozen, and it is better on day two than day one. Reheat it covered over medium heat with a splash of water until it bubbles, then poach fresh eggs into it. Poached eggs do not keep, so only crack as many as the table will eat.

recipes.title: Abendbrot
recipes.summary: Bread, cheese, eggs and cold vegetables, all of it on the table at once so everyone builds their own supper. Five minutes of arranging and no heat at all.

steps.text: Take the butter out of the fridge before anything else so it is spreadable by the time you sit down. Cold butter tears the bread, and the bread is the floor the whole meal stands on.
Slice the bread thicker than you would for a sandwich, six or eight slices, and leave the rest of the loaf out with the knife beside it so a second round does not mean a trip back to the kitchen.

Stir the chives into the cream cheese and put it in a small dish with its own knife. Slice the gouda thin and lay the slices overlapping rather than stacked, so taking one does not knock over the pile.

Cut the cucumber into coins, halve the radishes so the cut sides show, and slice the tomatoes thick. Salt the tomatoes on their own plate and leave them for five minutes, which is the whole difference between a tomato and a garnish.
Peel the eggs, halve them lengthwise, and set them yolk side up with salt and plenty of pepper over them. Halved eggs get eaten; whole ones sit there all evening.

Give the pickles one small dish and the mustard another, each with its own spoon. Wet things sitting straight on the board soak the bread and are what makes a table look like leftovers instead of dinner.
Put the cold cuts on their own plate at one end of the table, not tucked in among the cheese, so whoever wants them can reach them and nobody else has to think about it.

Carry everything out in one go and spread it into small plates with space between them, nothing crowded and nothing stacked, then set a plate and a knife at every seat. No part of this is a course, so what makes it dinner is only that the table was laid on purpose.

recipes.title: Meze Plate
recipes.summary: Hummus, labneh, feta and cut vegetables on the table at once, with warm pita and nothing on the stove.

steps.text: Spread the hummus across a wide shallow bowl or plate, pushing it out to the rim with the back of a spoon and leaving a shallow well in the middle. Pour a tablespoon of the olive oil into the well and scatter the za'atar over the top.

Spoon the labneh into its own small bowl, smooth the top, and finish it with another tablespoon of olive oil and a pinch of the salt. Keeping it separate matters more than it sounds like it should, because anyone who only wants bread and labneh can have exactly that.

Put the feta on the board in one piece with the last of the olive oil over it, the red pepper flakes if you want them, and a knife alongside. A slab people break pieces off travels better than crumbles do.

Cut the cucumbers into spears rather than coins so they can be dipped, halve the tomatoes and the radishes, and set each one out in its own small dish or in its own stripe on the board. Salt the cucumbers and tomatoes lightly and tuck the lemon wedges in somewhere.
Add the olives in a bowl small enough that the pits have somewhere to go, and shower the parsley over the hummus and the vegetables.
Warm the pita for a minute or two in a dry pan, a toaster or the oven until it puffs and smells like bread again, then cut it into wedges and bring it to the table in a towel so it stays soft.

If anyone wants fish or meat, lay the sardines out in one small dish and the salami in another, each with its own fork, and put them on the table alongside everything else rather than on the board. That way the plate stays something all four people can eat from and whoever wants them takes them onto their own plate.

recipes.title: Grain Bowl
recipes.summary: The Sunday prep, assembled: grains, something roasted, something legume, a sauce, something sharp on top.

steps.text: Take stock of the fridge before you start. This is a formula rather than a list: a grain, something roasted, something legume, a sauce, and something sharp. Any one of the five can be whatever is actually in there, so read the quantities below as the shape of a bowl and not as a shopping trip.

Whisk the tahini with the juice of the lemon, the garlic, and a good pinch of the salt. It will seize up and go pale and stiff, which is correct. Add cold water a spoonful at a time, whisking, until it loosens and falls off the whisk in a ribbon.
Cover the sliced onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt in a small bowl and leave it alone while you do everything else. Twenty minutes turns it pink and takes the raw bite out of it.

Warm the roasted vegetables in a dry skillet over medium heat for a few minutes, until they stop being fridge cold. One warm component in an otherwise cool bowl is most of what makes this read as dinner rather than as leftovers.
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil and a pinch of salt so they are seasoned on their own. Halve the eggs. Crumble the feta. Chop the parsley.

Put every component on the table in its own bowl, with the grains and the sauce at one end and the pickled onion, feta, and parsley at the other. Nobody gets a plate someone else composed. The chicken, if you are using it, goes in its own bowl for whoever wants it.

Build in order so it works: grains first, then the warm vegetables, then the legume, then the sauce over all of it, then the sharp things last so they stay sharp. Dress only what you are about to eat, because a dressed bowl goes soft in the fridge and the undressed components keep for days.

recipes.title: Nicoise Plate
recipes.summary: Potatoes, green beans, boiled eggs, tomatoes, olives, and a bowl of tuna, all put out at once so everyone builds their own plate.

steps.text: Fill a large pot with water, salt it like pasta water, and bring it to a boil. One pot does the potatoes, then the eggs, then the beans, in that order.
Boil the potatoes until a knife slides into one with no resistance, 12 to 14 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon and leave the water on the heat.
Lower the eggs into the same water and cook them 9 minutes for a yolk that is set at the edge and still bright in the middle. Move them straight into cold water.
Drop the green beans into the pot and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until they are bright and still squeak when you bite one. Drain and run them under cold water so they hold their color.

While the pot works, whisk the mustard, vinegar, shallot, salt, and pepper in a bowl, then pour in the olive oil slowly, whisking, until it thickens. Make it sharper than tastes right on a spoon, because potatoes and eggs flatten a dressing.
Spoon a third of the vinaigrette over the potatoes while they are still warm, when they drink it in instead of shedding it.
Peel and halve the eggs. Break the tuna into a bowl and loosen it with a spoonful of vinaigrette and a squeeze of lemon.

Put everything on the table in its own bowl: potatoes, beans, eggs, tuna, tomatoes, olives, with the lettuce, capers, parsley, and the rest of the vinaigrette alongside. Everyone builds their own plate, so the tuna is one choice among six rather than the dinner. Boiled potatoes, eggs, and beans keep three days covered in the fridge, which makes the leftovers tomorrow's lunch.

recipes.title: Pasta Aglio e Olio
recipes.summary: Spaghetti, a head of garlic, and good oil. Nothing fresh required, and the tossing is the whole recipe.

steps.text: Boil water in the large pot and salt it well. Use a bit less water than usual, about four quarts for a pound, so it ends up starchier. That starch is the only thickener in this dish.

Slice the garlic as thin as your knife allows. Thin coins toast evenly and sweeten; minced garlic scorches in spots before the rest is ready, and scorched garlic is bitter in a way nothing later fixes.

Put the garlic and the oil in the cold skillet together, then set it over low heat. Let it come up slowly until the slices are barely pale gold at the edges and the oil smells sweet, three or four minutes. Stop there and slide the pan off the burner.
Stir the pepper flakes into the warm oil off the heat. If someone at the table wants no heat at all, spoon a little plain garlic oil into a bowl first and dress that portion with it at the end.
Boil the spaghetti one minute short of the time on the box, so it still has some spine. Dip out two cups of the water before you drain it, and do not skip this, because the sauce is made of it.

Set the skillet over medium heat, add the drained pasta and half a cup of the pasta water, and toss hard and without stopping for about a minute. The oil and water start out separate and thin, then turn into one glossy sauce that coats every strand. Splash in more water if it looks oily; keep tossing if it looks watery.
Off the heat, add the parmesan in two handfuls with a good toss between them. Off the heat matters here: in a hot pan the cheese tightens into strings instead of melting into the sauce.

Add the parsley if there is any in the house, taste for salt, and bring the pan to the table so everyone takes their own. Put the cheese and the parsley out alongside it too, for whoever wants more and whoever wants none.

recipes.title: Rice with a Fried Egg
recipes.summary: Hot rice, a crisp edged fried egg, and a shower of furikake, built from a shelf with nothing fresh on it.

steps.text: Rinse the rice in a few changes of cold water until the water runs nearly clear, then drain it well.
Put the rice in a saucepan with 2 and a quarter cups water and a big pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil, cover it, and turn the heat to low.
Cook undisturbed for 15 minutes, then pull the pan off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes more. The resting does real work, so do not peek.
While the rice rests, put the furikake, the soy sauce, the sesame oil, and the scallions on the table in small bowls so everyone seasons their own.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium high heat until it thins out and shimmers. There should be enough to pool, not just slick the pan.

Crack in as many eggs as fit without touching and leave them alone. The whites bubble, set, and go brown and lacy at the rim in about 2 minutes. Tilt the pan and spoon the hot oil over the whites until they are firm and the yolks still move.

Fluff the rice, bowl it up, and slide an egg onto each one. Everyone adds their own furikake, a few drops of soy sauce, a little sesame oil, and scallions, and it gets eaten while the edges are still crisp.

recipes.title: Pasta with Tomato and Tuna
recipes.summary: The tin never reaches the table. A garlicky tomato sauce gets the tuna folded in off the heat, in big flakes, and the sharp things stay in bowls on the side.

steps.text: Put a large pot of well salted water on to boil.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry small skillet over medium heat, shaking often, until they smell nutty and turn the color of sand. Tip them into a bowl for the table.

Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over low heat with the garlic and the pepper flakes. Keep the heat low enough that the garlic never colors, about 3 minutes. You want it soft and sweet, not toasted.

Add the tomatoes and the salt, bring it up to a lively simmer, and cook until a spoon dragged through the pan leaves a track that fills in slowly, 10 to 12 minutes. A jar of marinara stands in here; give it 5 minutes to thicken instead.
Boil the spaghetti until just short of tender. Save a mug of the water before you drain it.

Turn the heat off under the sauce. Add the tuna and the capers and fold them through in large flakes rather than stirring them smooth. The tuna is already cooked and only needs to warm, and the flakes are what keep this tasting like dinner rather than like a tin.

Add the drained pasta and a splash of the saved water and toss until the sauce coats every strand. Finish with the juice of half the lemon and the black pepper, then taste and add more lemon if it needs lifting.

Bring the parsley, the olives, and the toasted breadcrumbs to the table in their own small bowls instead of scattering them over the pan. That way one plate can be plain tomato pasta and the next can have all three, and nobody has to pick anything out.

recipes.title: Tuna Melt
recipes.summary: A grilled cheese that happens to have tuna in it. Everything comes off the pantry shelf.

steps.text: Drain the tuna hard, pressing it against the lid of the tin to get the last of the water out. Wet tuna steams the bread from the inside.
Flake it into a bowl with the mayonnaise, mustard, pickles, scallions, and pepper. You want it to hold together in a spoon, not slump.
Butter one side of all eight slices of bread. That side goes down against the pan, so it is the side that crisps.

Lay four slices buttered side down on a board. On each one put cheese, then tuna, then more cheese, and close it with a second slice, buttered side up. Cheese against both slices is what holds the sandwich shut.
If one of the children wants cheese and no tuna, build that one now. It cooks in the same pan for the same time and nobody has to discuss it.

Cook in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, pressing down now and then with a spatula, until the underside is deep gold, 4 to 5 minutes. Keep the heat low: hot and fast gives you a dark crust over cold cheese.
Flip and cook until the second side matches and the cheese has run out to the edges, 3 to 4 minutes more.
Let them sit a minute so the inside settles, then cut each one on the diagonal and put the halves on the table for people to take.

recipes.title: A Pot of Grains
recipes.summary: A component rather than a meal: a batch of farro or brown rice boiled, drained, and cooled so the week's bowls and plates have a base ready to go.

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot with the salt and the bay leaves. Cook the grain like pasta, in much more water than it can absorb, so it comes out in separate pieces instead of a block.
Rinse the grain under cold water until it runs clear, then tip it into the boiling water and keep it at a steady simmer, uncovered.

Simmer until tender with a little chew left in the center, about 25 minutes for farro and 35 for brown rice. Start tasting 5 minutes early, because a grain that goes soft now will be mush by Wednesday.
Drain in a colander, pull out the bay leaves, and shake the colander hard to throw off the water sitting between the grains.

Spread the grain over a sheet pan in a thin layer and toss it with the olive oil. The thin layer is what lets the steam leave, and steam trapped in a warm covered bowl is what turns a good batch sour by Tuesday. Leave it 20 minutes, until it is no warmer than the room.
Squeeze over the lemon if the grain is headed for salads and cold bowls, and leave it plain if it is going under something saucy.

Pack the cooled grain into a container, loosely rather than pressed down, and refrigerate within the hour. It keeps 5 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer, frozen flat in meal size bags. Cold from the fridge it goes straight into bowls and salads with no reheating at all. To serve it hot, put it in a pan with a splash of water, cover, and warm over medium heat for 3 or 4 minutes, or microwave it covered with a damp paper towel on top. Both work because the trick is steam, and grain reheated dry comes back hard.

recipes.title: Hard Boiled Eggs
recipes.summary: Six eggs boiled to a set yolk, chilled hard in ice water, and kept in the shell all week.

steps.text: Put enough water in a saucepan to cover the eggs by an inch, leave the eggs out of it for now, and bring it to a full rolling boil. Starting them in boiling water rather than cold is what makes the timing repeatable, because the clock starts at a temperature you can see.
While it heats, fill a mixing bowl with cold water and as much ice as it will hold. This is half the recipe, so do not skip it or make it lukewarm.

Lower the eggs in one at a time on a spoon so they do not crack against the bottom. Add the baking soda if you are using it, which nudges the water alkaline and helps the shells let go later. Bring the heat back to a steady gentle boil.

Boil 11 minutes for a yolk that is set through and still yellow rather than grey. For other yolks: 7 minutes jammy in the middle, 9 minutes set at the edge and soft in the center, 13 minutes firm and crumbly.

Lift them straight into the ice bath and leave them 10 minutes, until they are cold all the way to the middle. Any time spent warm after the boil keeps cooking the yolk and sets the shell against the white.

Dry them and keep them in the fridge in the shell, where they hold a week. Peel one at a time as you want it, under cold running water if the shell fights you. Once peeled they are best within two days, so peel for the board or the plate, not for the week.

recipes.title: A Pot of White Beans
recipes.summary: Cannellini braised soft in olive oil, garlic, bay and lemon peel, good enough to eat on toast on their own and the base for half the week besides.

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over low heat with the garlic, the bay leaf and a wide strip of lemon peel cut off with a vegetable peeler. Hold it at a lazy sizzle for about 5 minutes, until the garlic smells sweet. It should not brown; if it starts to, pull the pot off the heat for a minute.

Add the beans, the broth and the salt. The liquid should just cover the beans, so top it up with water if it does not. Starting from dried instead: soak a pound overnight, simmer them in plenty of unsalted water with the same garlic, bay and peel for an hour to an hour and a half until a bean crushes against the roof of your mouth, salt them in the last 20 minutes, and carry on here with their own cooking liquid in place of the broth.

Bring it up to the barest simmer, one bubble at a time, and leave it uncovered for 25 minutes with a gentle stir once or twice. The beans drink up the garlic and lemon and the liquid thickens into something between a broth and a sauce.

Fish out the bay leaf and the strip of peel. Crush a big spoonful of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them back in, which is what makes the liquid creamy without any cream. Then taste it properly: it wants more salt than you think, a squeeze of the lemon, a grind of pepper and a last pour of raw olive oil.

Eat them warm, spooned onto thick toast with parsley and a pinch of chili flakes for whoever wants it, and put the bowl on the table so everyone takes their own. They keep 5 days covered in the fridge, sitting in their liquid, which is what stops them drying out, and they improve on day two. Reheat a portion gently in a small pan with a splash of water until just steaming; a hard boil breaks the skins. They also freeze in their liquid for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: A Sheet Pan of Roasted Vegetables
recipes.summary: The Sunday pan that feeds the rest of the week. A method rather than a fixed list, so it works on whatever the shop had.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425F. That number matters more than anything else here: much lower and the vegetables give up their water and steam in it, much higher and thin edges are black before the middles are done. Put the rack in the upper third of the oven.

Treat the ingredient list as a suggestion and use what is in the house. Autumn and winter: carrots, sweet potato, squash, potato, fennel, cauliflower, brussels sprouts halved through the root. Spring and summer: zucchini, peppers, broccoli, green beans, whole cherry tomatoes. Aim for about three pounds, which is one full pan, and no more than three or four kinds, or it turns into a medley nobody picks from.

Cut each vegetable so that its own pieces match, not so that all the vegetables match. Dense roots want 1 inch pieces, broccoli and cauliflower want florets about the same size, onion wants wedges thick enough to hold together. Peel the broccoli stems and slice them; they are the best part of the pan and get thrown away more often than not.

Toss in a bowl with the oil, salt, and pepper until every surface is glossy, about a tablespoon of oil per pound. Dry patches will scorch rather than brown. Salt now, not after; it has thirty minutes to get somewhere. Tuck in the garlic cloves if you want them, skins on, so they steam into something spreadable instead of burning.

Spread everything on the pan in one layer with a little bare metal showing between the pieces, flat cut sides down against the pan. This is the whole trick. Vegetables touching each other trap steam and go grey and soft, and browning only happens where a cut face meets hot metal. If the pan is crowded, use two pans on two racks rather than one tall pile.

Roast 25 to 35 minutes and leave them alone for the first 20, which is when the undersides set their crust. Then turn the pieces once and look at the pan rather than the clock. They are done when the edges are deeply browned in patches and a knife tip slides into a root with no resistance at all. Tender but pale means they need longer; a little char on a floret is flavour, not a mistake. Soft, quick vegetables like zucchini or tomatoes only need the last 15 minutes, so add them late or give them their own pan.
Taste one, add salt if it needs it, and squeeze the lemon over while the pan is still hot. Acid goes further into hot vegetables than cold ones.

Cool them uncovered on the pan so the steam has somewhere to go, then refrigerate in a shallow container for up to 5 days. They are genuinely good cold, eaten straight from the box, piled into pita with hummus, or tipped over grains with a spoonful of sauce, so cold is a real answer and not a compromise. To bring them back hot, spread them on a hot pan at 425F for 6 to 8 minutes or crisp them in a dry skillet. The microwave works but makes them limp.

recipes.title: Tahini Lemon Sauce
recipes.summary: A jar of this turns three cold things in the fridge into dinner. Makes about a cup and a half.

steps.text: Grate the garlic into a small bowl and squeeze both lemons over it. Leave it while you find the jar. Ten minutes in the juice takes the raw edge off the garlic.
Put the tahini in a bowl with the salt and the cumin if you are using it, then pour the lemon and garlic in. For a milder jar, pour it through a small strainer and leave the garlic behind.
Whisk, and watch it seize into a stiff pale paste that looks broken. It is not broken. That is what tahini does the moment it meets acid, and it means you are where you should be.

Add the ice water a tablespoon at a time, whisking hard after each one. The paste slackens, goes the color of cream, and turns glossy. Stop when it runs off the whisk in a slow ribbon, somewhere near half a cup of water, though every tahini drinks a different amount.
Taste it and push it where it needs to go: salt if it reads flat, lemon if it reads heavy, another spoon of water if it is stiffer than you want.
Scrape it into the jar. It keeps a week in the fridge and stiffens as it sits, so whisk in a spoonful of cold water to bring it back before it goes on anything.
